Platform team2030-05-14

Send notifications through a queue

In review

Notifications leave the web request and go out from a queue, so that a slow mail server never slows a page.

Conclusion

  1. Which queueA table in the database we haveIt needs no new service to run, and the load is well within what the database takes
  2. How to try a failed send againUndecided

Background

Today a notification is sent inside the web request that causes it: saving a comment sends its email before the page answers. When the mail provider is slow, so is the page, and a provider outage turns into failed saves.

Last month 2% of comment saves took over five seconds, all of them waiting on the mail provider.

Goals

  • A page answers without waiting for any notification
  • A notification that fails is tried again, and none is lost
  • Email, push and chat go out the same way

Non-goals

  • Changing what the notifications say
  • A user's settings of which notifications they get

Options

Which queue

A table in the database we have Recommended
  • Pro: No new service to run or watch
  • Pro: Written in the same transaction as the comment
  • Con: Polling adds load to the database
A message broker
  • Pro: Made for this, and scales further
  • Con: A new service to run, watch and back up

How to try a failed send again

Back off exponentially

1 minute, then 2, 4 and on, up to a day.

A fixed delay

Every 5 minutes, up to 50 times.

Decided

  • A notification is written to the queue in the same transaction as what causes it
  • Workers take at most 20 notifications at a time
  • A notification still failing after a day is kept, marked dead, for a person to look at

Impact

AreaEffect
Web appWrites to the queue instead of sending; answers faster
DatabaseA new table notifications, polled by the workers
OperationsTwo worker processes to deploy and watch

Rollout

  1. Write to the queue and send in the request

    Both ways for a week, comparing what goes out.

  2. Send from the workers only
  3. Remove the sending from the web app
